newsitem.title: UK: BAe confirms seeking new German naval deal.
newsitem.headline: BAe confirms seeking new German naval deal.

text.p: British Aerospace Plc said on Tuesday it was in discussions with three German companies and the receiver of former Bremer Vulkan unit STN Atlas Electronik to seek opportunities for expanding its naval systems activities possibly through collaboration with German partners.
In a statement BAe said it was talking to Rheinmetall, Mannesman AG and Wegmann, as well as the STN Atlas receiver.
The announcement confirmed a report in Tuesday's Financial Times that BAe was interested in STN Atlas.
The statement provided no other details of the ways in which BAe might link up with STN, which makes torpedoes and weapons control systems as well as marine electronics, including sonar and radars.
According to the FT report, the British company is expected to take a stake of up to 49 percent in STN, though this was not confirmed in the statement.

The paper said STN had sales of 1.45 billion marks last year and made net profits of 32.5 million marks, and that the receiver was eager to close a deal soon that gets between 400 and 800 million marks for the business.
